1324.d:
A generative take on the techniques of Damien Hirst’s famous Spin paintings.

Each spin painting is unique, but share a common algorithm. 

This work is about translating a real-world painting technique into digital , generative form. Unique blends of colour and shape are created by generatively assigning each work a set of traits that guide the process. The number of rotations, brush sizes, colour palettes and framing all add to the result. 

Traits:
Blend mode – 5 different modes for blending colour
Density – how many brushes 
Colours – 5 different palettes
Spin count – how many spins to create the piece
Spin direction – what direction it spins
Frame – Mostly white, but also a rare special tunnel effect 

Press S to save a ipg of the resulting image

For my first ever generative art I wanted to solve the Circle packing problem using a simple but effective way based in the nature.

For each interaction, one circle is added in a random position and the rest of the universe grows one unit each time.
This universe is continuously expanding, resize the window and see what happens.

The uniqueness of each piece is also made by the color representation:
- Color palette: Pick one (or more, until 5!) from 200 curated color palettes to represent the universe.
- Background color: From the merged palette, the algorithm choose one of the colors randomly and create a variation of the luminosity increasing or decreasing a few steps, so every circle can be visible.

Who is going to get the biggest universe of the set in the first 40 seconds of the conception? Mint a piece and let figure it out together!

1408.d:
1. Remember to stay focused on your dilemma or subject or question when casting.

2. Hold the lines loosely in your hands, shake them briefly, and then toss them, all the while contemplating your query. The line you record is determined by assigning numerical values to heads and tails, then adding the total. 

3. Collect the lines and toss another n times, recording the numerical values and the corresponding line each time, building your n+1-line hexagram from the bottom up.

Hommáge to S. L.

1445.d:
Hexaëder (cube) is a research into abstraction and a search for a balance between simplification and visual complexity.

No matter how simple and unambiguous things appear to be, in reality they are often more complex. Enjoy the simple, explore the complex.

Hexaeder has a wide variety of possible outcomes. I have put together 10 different color palettes; the number of cubes ranges from 10 to 401 (18 different grids); each cell can have 4 different background patterns; each cube can be filled in 4 distinct ways; there are 5 line colors and 16 different "cube figures"; the vignette can be black or be the color of the palette, and there are several "texture settings". This results in over 1.8 million possibilities.

For more information see: https://www.behance.net/gallery/131114761/Hexaeder-Flattened-cubes
